extension.summary: A departure board for the aircraft outside your window
extension.description:
Turns a view of an airport into a split-flap departure board. Rather than listing everything in the sky, it shows what is happening right now: the airliner on final approach, and the one climbing out. Each row carries the airline's logo, where the flight came from and where it is going, the flight number and the aircraft type.
Three views, switchable: the board on its own, the board beside a radar, or the board beside a map with the coastline and the real runway layouts. In both split views the surrounding traffic is drawn dim and the aircraft on the board are picked out bright, so the row that says LANDING and the aeroplane on the screen are obviously the same one. Set the compass bearing your window faces and the panel rotates to match, so straight up on screen is straight ahead through the glass.
Arrivals, departures and overflights are independent switches. Uses free, key-free public data: adsb.lol or adsb.fi for positions, adsbdb.com for airline and route lookups, or your own local dump1090/tar1090 receiver if you have one. No account and no API key required.
extension.news: v1.0.4 - Radar and map labels now use the same flight number the board prints, so a row and its aircraft can be matched up.
